prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer standing near a protruding white partition wall on the left (about 0.6–1.2 m away) looking past it into a sitting area where a round-edged dark object at the bottom of frames 1, 2, and 4 is within arm's reach (under 0.5 m). Beyond the partition, a blue accent chair sits at roughly 2.5–3 m in the center-left, a white cabinet and potted plant sit behind it at about 3.5–4 m, and a white couch lies to the right at 3.5–4.5 m, about 1–1.5 m across a glass coffee table from the chair. No other people are present in the scene, though the wearer's fingertips briefly appear at the very bottom edge of frames 1 and 2 behind the rim of the foreground object. Across the 5 frames, the camera stays roughly stationary in frames 1 and 2, tilts upward and rolls right in frame 3 (bringing the wall and exposed ceiling pipes into view while cropping the foreground object), returns downward in frame 4, and turns sharply left in frame 5 to face a white open shelving unit holding vases and a spherical wire decor piece within arm's reach (0.5–0.8 m). The depth map clearly separates the near partition wall plane and foreground container from the recessed sitting room in a way that flat white wall textures in RGB obscure, but it is unreliable on thin wire chair legs, the transparent glass coffee table, and the far sunlit window wall, which disappear into uniform dark background values.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete furniture and decor across the two zones: in frames 1–4 it detects the midground blue accent chair (2.5–3 m away, center-left), the white couch to its right (3.5–4.5 m away, separated by ~1.5 m), a background potted plant (~4 m away, above and behind the chair), and the dark rounded foreground object at the bottom of frames 2 and 4 (under 0.5 m, within the wearer's arm's reach, labeled as a chair). In frame 3, as the camera tilts up and rolls right, it additionally segments the second blue chair (~3.5 m away) partially occluded behind the nearer blue chair, while the couch is mostly cropped out at the bottom right. In frame 5, after the wearer turns left toward the nearby shelving unit (0.5–0.8 m away), only a single mask appears on the lower shelf's dark wire sphere, while the shelf structure, books, and top-shelf vases go unsegmented. This map makes it easier than RGB alone to distinguish the two overlapping dark-blue chairs in frame 3 and to track individual object footprints across the heavy camera roll, though it gives no metric depth or room geometry. It is unreliable in several places: the foreground object is missed entirely in frame 1 and mislabeled as a chair in frames 2 and 4, distant background objects in frame 2 are erratically labeled as vase and potted plant, the second background chair is missed in frames 1, 2, and 4, and the wire decor in frame 5 is misclassified as a clock.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, confirming that no other people are standing or sitting in the room or facing the camera wearer across the sequence. In frame 4, a single small yellow skeletal fragment appears in the lower-right area corresponding to the midground floor and chair legs roughly 2.5–3 m in front of the wearer. While the RGB image shows the brief tips of the camera wearer's fingers at the bottom center of frames 1 and 2 (within 0.3 m, partially occluded by the bottom frame boundary), the pose map fails to detect any magenta hand keypoints there. Compared to RGB alone, the pose map provides nothing useful here because the scene contains no visible human bodies, and it is unreliable both by missing the wearer's visible fingertips in frames 1–2 and by hallucinating a false-positive yellow body skeleton on the angled gold legs of the blue chair in frame 4.
